verdict.line: You lose if Aatrox lands his W (Infernal Chains) into a full Q combo before level 6; you win once Black Cleaver and Executioner's Calling let you out-trade and execute him with R.

brief.thesis: Aatrox is melee with a 825-range pull (W, Infernal Chains) and a self-healing dash (E, Umbral Dash), while Urgot's entire kit — Q at 800 range, W at 490, E at 475 — is built to fight from outside that pull radius. OP.GG's 50.2% head-to-head over 1760 games and the measured lane/solo-kill edge for Aatrox both come from the same window: levels 1-5, before Urgot's W (Purge) cooldown drops low enough to matter and before any armor shred or grievous wounds exists to blunt his all-in and sustain.

theirWindow.when: his W (Infernal Chains) lands on you
theirWindow.what: Once Infernal Chains hooks you to the impact point you're in range for his full Q (The Darkin Blade) swing sequence and a Deathbringer Stance-empowered auto. Use Flash or E (Disdain) immediately to get back outside 475-800 range rather than trading autos in the pull.

yourWindow.when: his W (Infernal Chains) just missed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With Infernal Chains down for 20/18/16/14/12s depending on his rank, he has no way to close the gap except E (Umbral Dash). Step up and land Q (Corrosive Charge) poke for free, since he can't punish you without burning that dash on cooldown.

start.why: 87% pick rate at 50.9% WR — the AD and sustain let you trade Q pokes without losing the all-in race before level 3.

boots.why: 69.6% pick at 50.7% WR; Aatrox's damage is entirely physical (Q, autos, Deathbringer's bonus is the only magic component), so flat physical reduction blunts both his poke and his all-in.

core.why: Armor shred from repeated Q and Purge hits strips his tankiness and the haste lowers your W (Purge) cooldown faster.
The shield and tenacity directly answer the Q+W all-in window — it's the item that turns a losing level 3-5 fight into a survivable one.
Highest-winning path (60.7% over 178 games); stacking resistances scale as fights drag into mid-game skirmishes.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards landing consecutive hits at range before he closes the gap — exactly the poke pattern Q (Corrosive Charge) and auto-attacks need to win the pre-6 window.

summoners.why: Exhaust+Flash runs the highest measured WR (53.1%) and directly answers the thing that kills you in this matchup — it cuts both the damage and the healing on his Q+W all-in. Flash+Ignite (86% pick, 50.1% WR) is the standard default if you'd rather threaten early kills yourself.

playing.title: Hold outside 825 range
playing.detail: Infernal Chains reaches further than any of your abilities. Pre-6, never stand where a landed W lets him chain into a full Q sequence.

playing.title: Track his W cooldown, not his HP
playing.detail: Infernal Chains is his only long-range engage. When it's down (20/18/16/14/12s by rank), he can only reach you with E (Umbral Dash), which you can out-trade at range.

playing.title: Don't contest solo all-ins before level 6
playing.detail: The measured solo-kill advantage favors him in exactly this window — play for minions and poke, not for a duel.

playing.title: Buy Executioner's Calling before forcing fights
playing.detail: His passive and E both heal him; grievous wounds is what makes your damage actually stick in extended trades.

playing.title: Save E (Disdain) as a punish, not an opener
playing.detail: Disdain shields you and displaces the first champion it catches — hold it to answer his E dash-in rather than leading with it.

playing.title: Finish with R once he's low and sustain is cut
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death's execute threshold is easiest to close once Executioner's Calling removes his Umbral Dash heal — this is the kill pattern OP.GG's own notes point to.

playing.title: Let Purge rank up before trading sustained
playing.detail: W starts at a 12s cooldown; it's not a real trading tool until rank 3+ drops it to 6s or lower.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, win rates, and pick rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning — why the all-in window exists and how to play around it — is my own read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Focus on keeping your distance from his (Q)-(E) combo. After purchasing Executioner’s Calling, make sure [E] lands successfully and kill him off with [R].
